Key Activities: Plans, organizes, conducts and participates in evaluation studies related to Statistics Canada programs, policies and initiatives to evaluate their relevance and performance, under the supervision of the Evaluation Manager.

Identifies and recommends evaluation frameworks; formulates evaluation project plans in conjunction with the Evaluation Manager and recommends the objectives, scope, schedules, budgets, criteria, methodologies, data gathering instruments and terms of reference of studies; recommends study approaches, results indicators and study designs.

Researches, identifies and selects information for evaluations from a variety of sources; analyzes information related to Statistics Canada business lines, policy, program performance, program relevance, success and cost-effectiveness.

Develops and/or carries out specific elements of Statistics Canada evaluation projects such as: conducting literature and data research; identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; participating in the conduct of interviews and focus groups; and applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions.

Assesses current and future requirements for data related to evaluation and performance measurement; interprets and analyzes information to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of Statistics Canada evaluation studies.

Analyzes and interprets the results of evaluation studies and projects conducted with Statistics Canada clients, and OGDs, partners and stakeholders in order to analyze the relevance and performance of programs of Statistics Canada; and conducts follow-up interviews to clarify or expand information obtained from evaluation studies.

Develops evaluation reports, briefings and presentations outlining results of evaluation studies; develops options, strategies and recommendations, and provides advice and recommendations to the Evaluation Manager and Director to improve the effectiveness of policies, programs and services.

Consults and works collaboratively with other government departments, partners and stakeholders when conducting evaluation studies and projects; represents Statistics Canada at internal and external meetings to discuss various aspects of evaluation studies; and shares best practices in the evaluation field.

Communication:: Oral and written skills are required to present and explain to Statistics Canada program and departmental managers, the findings, conclusions and recommendations from evaluations and other studies, in order to gain acceptance and implementation of recommendations. The subject matter is diverse and technical information can be complex.

Oral presentation skills are required to explain to Statistics Canada program managers and staff, or project team members, issues related to evaluation processes, practices, plans and methodologies, result-based measurement, management, processes and practices, to obtain cooperation throughout the project phases and ultimately to gain acceptance of study findings, conclusions and recommendations.

Consultation and liaison skills are required to establish and maintain a variety of networks within and outside of the Federal government to participate on departmental and interdepartmental committees, seminars, workshops and task forces with individuals from a variety of disciplines and knowledge levels. This involves discussing and resolving issues, working partnerships, gaining and maintaining the acceptance of members, and developing strong working relationships.
Strong written skills are required to develop and prepare evaluation reports, papers, briefing notes, presentations and Ministerial correspondence.
Knowledge of Specialized Fields:: Knowledge is required of program evaluation theories, processes and practices for conducting evaluation studies and development of evaluation frameworks related to studies. This knowledge is required to plan, organize and conduct program evaluation studies and to develop, options, strategies and recommendations based on studies conducted.

Knowledge of theories and principles of economics, sociology, social sciences, demography and statistics to: plan, direct and coordinate economic and socio-economic analysis of programs to evaluate their effectiveness against organizational strategic objectives; formulate and provide recommendations on agency policies, and direct the application of statistical and quantitative analysis. Knowledge of socio-economic trends in Canada and their impact on Statistics Canada programs.

Knowledge of program evaluation methodologies, including planning tools such as terms of reference, statements of work and requests for proposals; as well as logic models, comparative analyses, profiles, case studies, and data collection instruments (focus sessions, interviews, and surveys). These skills are required to define and recommend approaches to evaluations and to plan and conduct the evaluation process.

Knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of research is required, including: hypothesis formulation and validation; model design and interpretation, experimental and comparative study designs; surveys, simulations, interviews, focus groups, file reviews and case studies; qualitative and quantitative analysis, including statistical sampling and cost-benefit analysis; computer assisted analysis packages; survey questionnaire design; and the strengths and weaknesses of these methods, tools and techniques in order to recommend and select project methodologies.
Contextual Knowledge:: Knowledge of Statistics Canada’s structure, organization, mandate, vision, business lines, program structure, organizational hierarchy and priorities in order to: identify evaluation issues and conduct program evaluations; contribute meaningful results on individual evaluations; provide input to strategic and operational business plans; and develop recommendations.

Knowledge of central agency policies and guidelines concerning program evaluation in order to recommend the objectives and approaches for program evaluations. Knowledge is required of policies, practices and guidelines related to central agencies and Parliament accountability and reporting requirements. This knowledge is required to recommend evaluation and performance measurement frameworks.
Knowledge of the Statistics Act to understand the legislative requirements under which the agency operates such as the need to ensure the confidentiality of all information provided to it.

Knowledge of other federal department programs that are affected by, or have an impact on Statistics Canada programs and policies in order to understand and evaluate the context in which Statistics Canada and its programs operate and to collaborate on inter-departmental evaluation studies and projects.

Knowledge of partners and stakeholders (including various provincial or territorial statistical organizations) who are affected by or who have an impact on departmental programs and policies to evaluate their impact on the agency.

Knowledge of emerging trends and developments in the Canadian private sector, academia and non-governmental organizations, as well as statistical programs of foreign governments in order to facilitate appropriate analysis.

Knowledge of government and departmental regulations, policies and legislation as they apply to evaluation program activities, issues, processes and methods. These include the Public Service Values and Ethics Code, the Policy on Results and its related directives and standards (Mandatory Procedures for Departmental Results Frameworks, Program Inventories, Performance Information Profiles and Programs, Mandatory Procedures for Evaluation, Standard on Evaluation, Standard on Mandatory Outcomes and Performance Indicators, Standard on Tagging), the Financial Administration Act, the Federal Accountability Act, Privacy and Access to Information Acts, Official Languages Act, Public Opinion Research and the Management Accountability Framework. This is required to understand the impact of legislation, regulations and interrelationships with other federal / provincial / territorial legislation.
Research and Analysis:: Assesses current and future requirements for data; interprets and analyzes information to support findings and conclusions for evaluations conducted; analyzes, assesses and synthesizes information from a variety of sources in order to carry out evaluations of programs and policies.

Analytical skills are required to assimilate and integrate evaluation studies to arrive at innovative solutions and recommendations for future actions and direction, including improvements to Statistics Canada policies, programs and services.

Analytical skills are required to analyze the results of studies and projects conducted with Statistics Canada’s clients, OGDs, partners and stakeholders to examine relevance and performance of programs.

Analytical skills are required to recommend evaluation frameworks and terms of reference for evaluations, which includes the need to conceptualize and identify potential evaluation issues and results indicators, and propose appropriate study designs. As well, there is a requirement to quickly understand the key elements of the program or initiative, to the extent that a solid working hypothesis can be developed, and to remain flexible to the evolving information flow and potential shifts in direction as the project proceeds.

The scope of work is determined in conjunction with the Evaluation Manager. There is a requirement to determine information to be utilized in evaluation studies. Information is obtained from a variety of sources including: interviews and focus groups with departmental managers, employees and stakeholders; Acts and Regulations as well as socio-economic and scientific documents; publications and conferences related to policy and government machinery issues. There is a requirement to recommend areas for further review based on studies conducted.

Adapts methods and techniques used in program evaluation to meet requirements. There is also a need to determine the impact of variables on studies conducted. Such variables include: emerging trends and developments in the provincial / territorial data systems, as well as developments in the Canadian private sector, academia and NGOs.

Key Activities: Conducts research and analysis into economic trends, policy and initiative issues, reviews planning and management policies and standards and submits program evaluation reports and documents.

Provides consultative services to departmental clients related to strategic, annual and long-term evaluation plans, priority setting, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting.

Develops and recommends strategies to assist departmental managers to effectively integrate program evaluation methodologies into the design and implementation of programs, policies, and initiatives.

The Planning, Evaluation and Resource Management Division is the Office of Modern Comptrollership which provides direction and expertise on the development and implementation of  the MAF (Management Accountability Framework).

Prepares reports on business requirements along with recommendations on alternative solutions to meet those requirements and provides assistance in the design of appropriate business and financial planning processes, strategies and plans to support the integration of strategic business needs.

Conducts evaluation projects to assess the impact, effectiveness, efficiency and relevance of departmental and interdepartmental programs, policies and initiatives and participates in the Strategic Streamlining Process by helping managers identify and achieve program efficiencies.
Develops evaluation standards and performance indicators as well as procedures for monitoring and reporting purposes.

Job Content Knowledge Application\n\n: Knowledge of statistical methods and techniques to conduct research and analysis into economic trends, policy and initiative issues; to collect and analyze foundation data in order to create new information about programs and their effectiveness; to select data sources to be used; and to develop and gather information which will be used by management to make informed decisions concerning the scope, structure, redefinition or termination of major programs, initiatives, operations or activities.
Knowledge of concepts, methods and techniques to develop evaluation standards and performance indicators as well as procedures for monitoring and reporting purposes.

Knowledge is required of computer software applications to conduct analysis and document project results, including specialized software such as statistical sampling, computer assisted techniques, automated working papers, and flowcharting.

Knowledge of social science research methods, techniques and practices, including multi-disciplinary analysis methods, to carry out analysis on a variety of approaches regarding performance and accountability framework in other levels of government, other jurisdictions and in the private sector.

Skill in synthesising information from diverse disciplines (management science, economics, and public policy administration, etc.) to facilitate the development and the implementation of interdepartmental performance frameworks.
Knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of consultation, management, conflict resolution, small group process, interviewing and counselling to lead project teams, to negotiate contracts for services and agreements with other institutions.

Contextual Knowledge
OWN WORK UNIT:
Knowledge is required of the organization and objectives of the evaluation division; the strategic direction, culture, structure and organization, mandate, objectives, policies, procedures and work tools of the Field, branch, division; and the structure and organization of project work teams, their mandates and objectives. This knowledge is required to achieve operational objectives and results in an effective and efficient manner, and to recommend new or improved business services, policies, systems and procedures.

Knowledge of the policies, procedures, guidelines, mandate and personnel of the Branch to provide consultative services related to strategic, annual and long-term evaluation plans, priority setting, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting; and to develop and recommend strategies to assist departmental managers to effectively integrate program evaluation methodologies into the design and implementation of programs, policies, and initiatives.

OWN DEPARTMENT OR AGENCY:
Knowledge of the policies, procedures, guidelines, mandate and personnel of the department to prepare program evaluation reports and documents on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of existing programs, operations and initiatives; to monitor and assess management accountability for departmental programs; and to recommend ways to improve departmental policies, programs and operations.

OTHER FEDERAL DEPARTMENTS AND AGENCIES:
Knowledge of the personnel, organization, priorities, policies, mandate, objectives, goals and programs of a wide range of client departments and organizations to provide advice and guidance regarding the development and implementation of reporting and performance review frameworks, processes and tools.

Knowledge is required of the Parliamentary system and machinery of government, and its expectations for the Department, policy making and legislative processes, government priorities, and  current and emerging management  issues; the mandate, policies, programs, operations and reporting processes of Parliamentary committees, central agencies, and other federal government departments; and the role of Treasury Board and the Privy Council Office.

CANADIAN PRIVATE SECTOR AND OTHER PUBLIC SECTORS:
Knowledge of personnel and organisation of different orders of government (provincial, territorial, municipal), the academic community, and non-government organisations in order to effectively communicate on performance and accountability approaches, methods, theories, studies, and analysis for the purpose of strengthening performance reporting to Parliament and the public.

Knowledge of think tanks that are working in the area of citizen engagement, societal indicators and quality of life modelling, to carry out analysis regarding alternative performance and accountability frameworks and approaches (e.g. National Statistical Council).

INTERNATIONAL PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTOR:
Knowledge of personnel and organisation of different national governments, international organisations (International Statistical Agencies), the international academic community, and non-government organisations in order to effectively communicate on performance and accountability approaches, methods, theories, studies, and analysis for the purpose of strengthening performance reporting to Parliament and the public.

FLEGISLATION AND REGULATIONS:
Knowledge of certain sections of legislation related to client departments and to STC reporting and reviews regulations and requirements. This knowledge is required to handle and process sensitive information and documentation related to client departments and reporting processes.

COMMUNICATION IN:
Listening and evaluation skills to interpret verbal and non-verbal communication when receiving information and feedback from colleagues, managers and departments to determine what their concerns are, to retain salient points and synthesize information on a variety of issues of differing complexity, and to understand opinion and points of view.
Reading and listening skills, to maintain knowledge of key developments, research and innovations related to reporting and accountability processes and techniques, to attend conferences and meetings of professional associations related to auditing, financial analysis, and accountability reporting, to analyse and assess a wide range of alternative accountability approaches, strategies and processes, to liase and consult with academics, researchers and related specialists regarding a wide range of issues and innovations.

B.  COMMUNICATION OUT:
Oral and written skills to make presentations and to consult with managers from client departments and organizations regarding strategic, annual and long-term evaluation plans, priority setting, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting.

Key Activities: Supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R, E-Views, SPSS or other similar software.
Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.
Organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies. Maintains work files.
Attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information.
Participates in project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis, and other unit activities.

activities, skills, responsibilities and: Communication skills are required to maintain networks across the branch and the federal community of practice to share best practices in advanced analytics.
Provides advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets.

Writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science. Information must be impartial and clearly presented to minimize the potential for misinterpretation.

As assigned, discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur.

There is a requirement to liaise with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development, and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs.

The work requires knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence, and exploratory/ confirmatory, predictive analysis, regression, text mining, and qualitative analysis. This knowledge is required to optimize the use of the Statistics Canada’s data assets and to provide leading edge thinking and methodologies to data analytics.

The work requires knowledge of the theories, principles, practices, and methodologies of statistics and mathematics in order to conduct the requisite modelling that provides meaningful information for policy and program decisions by management.

Knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies, data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis in order to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity.

Data literacy skills are needed to derive meaningful information from data, including the knowledge needed to read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data, as well as understand the use of data in decision-making. Data literacy includes data stewardship and the ability to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use. This is needed to develop briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data.

Basic knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of research is required including; hypothesis formulation and validation; model design and interpretation, experimental and comparative study designs; surveys, simulations, file reviews and case studies; qualitative and quantitative analysis including statistical sampling and cost benefit analysis; computer assisted analysis packages; and the strengths and weaknesses of these methods, tools and techniques in order to recommend and select project methodologies.

The work requires a basic knowledge of the mandate, vision, values, culture, organization, legislation, programs, business lines and operations of Statistics Canada. This is needed to ensure the alignment of the data analytics strategy with the department’s business intelligence requirements.

The work requires knowledge and understanding of the governance structures of Statistics Canada’s partnerships in order to assess data provided by other levels of government for validity and integrity.

Basic knowledge of Departmental, Central Agencies and Library and Archives Canada policies pertaining to the handling, tracking, filing and storing of sensitive and confidential material and information holdings, including electronic records.

Key Activities: Innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data.

Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs, new products, special studies, and ad hoc requests.
Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.
Provides specialized expertise and consultative services regarding production systems and processes for ongoing statistical program delivery.
Represents economic subject matter divisions on statistical development projects.
Occasionally leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.

Decision Making: Integrates input from multiple economic subject matter areas to develop and maintain complex systems and frameworks for the ongoing production, validation and dissemination of a range of specialized, high-impact statistical outputs.
Operationalizes specialized conceptual and measurement frameworks in the development of production, validation and dissemination systems, processes and databases.

Evaluates alternatives and develops and applies new strategies to maintain and improve operational systems, processes and databases in the production and dissemination of official statistics. Decisions and recommendations regarding data production and dissemination practices impact multiple projects and high-impact statistical programs.
Develops and implements quality-assurance processes for high-impact statistical outputs.

Investigates requirements for statistical information and analysis, defines the nature and scope of special studies, data requirements, and decides the methods and approaches to be used to satisfy complex data requirements. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.

Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources.  Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.
Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends and implements modifications and improvements to existing procedures.
Recommends and executes solutions to resolve complex technical issues pertaining to data production and dissemination that may lack precedents.
Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information, interprets preliminary results, reviews, and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary.
Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies, and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data.
Leadership And Operational Management: Occasionally plans, organizes and functionally coordinates the work of multiple partners within Statistic Canada divisions and units, as well as clients from other federal government departments involved in the conduct of statistical processing, validation and dissemination of specialized statistical outputs.  Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, plans and schedules the work and resolves conflicting priorities.
Establishes and coordinates schedules for the production, validation and dissemination of regular statistical outputs across multiple production teams.
Coordinates input and specifications from multiple partners to implement specialized solutions according to established production schedules in the context of complex statistical frameworks.
Communication: Provides expert advice and guidance to internal partners on statistical program results, dissemination methods, concepts, and techniques applied and on trends and developments in economic or related data programs. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic programs and other activities.
Interprets specialized information pertaining to a range of specialized subject matter areas to present arguments and options to clients within and outside the department.

Communicates subject matter concepts and technical definitions to internal contacts and other subject matter experts to explain and clarify current developments, to explain the results of studies, and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of data and the quality of outputs.
Specialized knowledge: Advanced knowledge of economic statistical frameworks, principles, and practices as they relate to a specialized subject matter area.

Advanced knowledge of theories, concepts, and principles in statistical measurement, and how they interrelate with at least one specialized economic subject matter area or discipline, is required to design, evaluate, and innovate systems and applications for the production, validation, and dissemination of high-impact statistical outputs. This knowledge is also required to provide subject-matter expertise, advice, and consultative services to Statistic Canada partners, as well as to work with other professionals, in the ongoing production and validation of high-impact statistical data.
In-depth knowledge and mastery in the application of specialized software, such as SAS, for the compilation, validation, and quality assurance of key statistical outputs.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work is required to incorporate them into the conduct and management of surveys and complex and technical studies and projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada is required to manage subject matter studies, surveys and projects across economic-based divisions. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise is also required to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances, and to recommend changes to other statistical programs if necessary.

In-depth knowledge of economics-related subject matter area(s) is required to understand complex data needs from internal and external data users and to deliver expert technical solutions in response to analytical requirements for statistical projects and programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of complex and technical statistical projects and activities.

Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements. Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector is required to identify potential new markets and to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act,  and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to others.  Knowledge of the Statistic and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
Research and analysis: Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations, and feasibility studies to produce data bases and data retrieval packages used for the production of integrated statistical information.

Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs.  Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a wide variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data has been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs. Assesses technical and conceptual problems and inconsistencies in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data and develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs.
Evaluates the impact of technological developments on operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines.

Research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria, and to ensure that processing systems yield desired statistical outputs.

Key Activities: Performs data integration, data manipulation, data analytics and in-depth analysis, towards producing dissemination and data visualization products using a variety of techniques and tools.
Develops recommendations, provides advice to management and implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data to meet user needs.

Provides specialized technical, advisory and consultative services.
Undertakes technical projects requiring data integration, data linkage and use of alternative data sources.
Participates in data acquisition negotiations.
May supervise employees directly or in a matrix environment to perform statistical processes, outputs or projects.

activities, skills, responsibilities and: Knowledge of statistical principles, theories and practices, to conduct comprehensive analysis for the purpose of producing reliable and relevant statistical data, and to provide subject-matter expertise, advice, and consultative services to stakeholders, in the ongoing production and validation of statistical data.
Basic knowledge of project management methods, principles and techniques for developing project objectives and timelines.

Knowledge of methods and techniques used in research, evaluation, manipulation, integration, analysis and dissemination of statistical data. This may include machine learning and other skills related to big data.
In-depth knowledge of applications of specialized software for the compilation, processing, classifying and validation of key statistical outputs.

Ability to communicate efficiently orally and in writing (i.e. analytical material, briefing notes, presentations), to understand user needs, to identify data linkage opportunities, to interpret results and synthesize messages.
Ability to research and analyze complex data sets, manipulate data and perform data linkage.
Ability to put data in broader socio-economic context and establish connections across statistical programs and cross-cutting topics.
Knowledge of divisional and organizational mandate, activities, priorities and practices applicable to the work.

Knowledge of statistical programs and products, including opportunities, limitations and potential policy impacts related to the area of expertise, in order to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to statistical programs if necessary.
Knowledge of subject matter areas and associated data needs in order to provide the highest quality data to be used in cross-cutting initiatives.
Understanding of the context of policies and practices of the government of Canada and Statistics Canada pertaining to publication, confidentiality and security of data as well as data quality.
Understanding of data suppliers and users, their needs and the current economic and political context in which they operate.
Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other relevant acts related to the subject matter areas, and of Statistics Canada policies.

Key Activities: Plan and conduct geographic data analysis (which may include geomatics, satellite photo reading and interpretation, etc.) and develop strategies, innovative methods, and models to produce, evaluate, analyze and develop geographic products; write and evaluate analytical geographic material for publication purposes (for internal or external use).
Provide specialized geospatial advisory and consultative services to users of geographic data within and outside of StatCan.

Perform detailed analyses, evaluations and reviews of methods and concepts related to administrative and statistical geographic areas to improve existing data and study the evolving client needs for administrative and statistical geographic areas.
May provide direct hierarchical supervision of one or more employees, or matrix supervision of teams responsible for geographic statistical products, projects or research studies.
Represent the division on geospatial development projects, study groups or committees in various capacities.

activities, skills, responsibilities and: Analyze and integrate data from different sources into geographic data and provide strategies to evaluate the conceptual geographic framework used.
Continuously evaluate different sources of geographic data to establish their relevance and accuracy when integrating them with statistical program data.
Knowledge of geographic principles, theories and practices related to specialized fields to perform statistical geographic data analysis to provide reliable and relevant statistical program data.

Knowledge of various industry sectors, classification systems, concepts and international reference frameworks to integrate multiple data sources and ensure the overall consistency and relevance of the statistical geographies produced.
Knowledge of quantitative analytical methods to integrate and interpret large volumes of data.

Basic knowledge of Statistics Canada's Departmental Project Management Framework (DPMF) as well as other methods, techniques and practices used in project management, human resources management and financial management to conduct projects and studies.

Knowledge in database management and analysis is essential, including the ability to design databases for geographic information systems projects, manipulate data within databases by constructing, modifying, integrating, extracting, and validating information, as well as effectively querying database management systems to analyze data and generate products. Additionally, a solid understanding of conceptual frameworks, geographic methods, and procedures relevant to the work.

Knowledge of data users and providers from various levels of government and the private sector, to provide advice on the geographic data outputs from statistical programs, discuss data communication agreements and ensure that their needs are understood.

Knowledge of national and international frameworks and their conceptual elements to contribute to the internal and international research program aimed at expending and improving compilation and delimitation concepts and methods.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and relevant legislation, as well as Statistics Canada policies, to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, organizations, industries, the general public and the media. Knowledge of the Statistics Act and the Privacy Act is especially important with respect to protecting the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that neither supervisors nor their direct subordinates release any information that could identify an individual or group without their prior consent.

Knowledge in Geographic Information System (GIS) and geomatics system development principles and practices, including service management, adherence to standard operating procedures, quality assurance, and testing protocols.
Knowledge in various programming languages (such as Python, R, SQL, HTML/CSS, Javascript) in geomatics to develop and offer comprehensive geomatics solutions and guidance.

Participate in meetings with professionals from other divisions, governmental departments and agencies, or international organizations to discuss current trends and new developments, acquire new knowledge on specialized geographic areas, regulations and policies relating to programs, and develop consensus on resolving key issues and setting priorities.

Present and describe the results of statistical geography programs and their practical application and interpretation for data users. This information is used to inform decision-making for a wide range of geographic programs and aspects.
Provide guidance to specialists in the field within and outside the organization, as well as to users of statistical geographic data.
Prepare, review and evaluate analytical material containing geographic elements to be published by Statistics Canada.
Plan and conduct comprehensive analyses and research covering multiple areas using administrative and statistical geography data.

Evaluate new geographic data sources, in accordance with related directives and policies, make updates and modifications to program content and coverage to align with international frameworks or classifications, and develop new concepts, definitions, methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and expand statistical geographic information relating to the different subject-matter areas.
As required, Coordinates recruitment activities, completion of employee performance evaluation, training, and assigning work to subordinate staff

Key Activities: Plans, prioritizes, coordinates, directs, monitors and undertakes the development, preparation, editing, validation and dissemination of statistical metadata and implements, directs and monitors statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes.

Provides expert assistance, advice and direction to internal clients, and to external clients within Canada, with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, determines changes in the needs of clients, assessing the impacts of these changes on statistical metadata programs and projects; establishes short-term plans and priorities.

Analyses and recommends options for modifying current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating metadata, develops recommended improvements by establishing project plans, priorities and target dates and directing and monitoring the activities of team members involved in the testing of new procedures and systems.

Directs the development of, evaluates, and approves documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; organizes and gives presentations; and coordinates and delivers training, establishing plans, priorities and target dates.

Develops and refines procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata; plans, directs and undertakes metadata quality evaluations; compiles and writes reports for clients and management; and presents results to senior management.

Leads project teams, supervises work units and participates as a statistical metadata representative in working groups, on development projects, tasks forces and committees in various leadership or expert roles such as Project Manager, Task Manager or Senior Advisor.

Communication: Provides expert advice and training with respect to the policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata to subordinates, other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers who use the information as input to on-going operations and to decisions concerning the management of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada and within other national organizations and agencies.

Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers at Statistics Canada to plan statistical metadata projects and implement short-term strategies for the development and enhancement of policies, procedures and methods used in the management of statistical metadata; to develop and translate strategies and requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; to establish project plans, priorities and target dates; to negotiate modifications to methods, procedures and timelines; to coordinate and deliver training, and to suggest improvements to methods, procedures and systems.

Writes detailed reports and prepares and delivers presentations which explain rationale, requirements and results relating to policies, directives, guidelines, methods and procedures used in the production, storage and dissemination of statistical metadata and which are used by other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients, and management in the operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management programs.

Writes reports which describe policy requirements related to the development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of high quality metadata, which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations and which make recommendations for procedures and tools that could be developed to evaluate the quality of statistical metadata. These reports are used by clients and management to ensure the quality and consistency of statistical metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and workgroups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of expertise.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Canada and internationally and knowledge of how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan, prioritize, coordinate, direct, monitor and undertake the preparation, editing, validation and quality evaluation of statistical metadata and short-term strategies for the enhancement of statistical metadata management processes

Advanced knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and the potential impacts of new or modified methods, procedures and systems on project teams and clients in order to plan, prioritize, coordinate, direct, monitor and undertake statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes; to recommend improvements to methods, procedures and training; to develop procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata; and to explain the results of metadata quality evaluations.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts, methods and techniques relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to evaluate client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination; to determine when changes in the needs of clients will impact statistical metadata programs and projects; and to more accurately and efficiently evaluate the quality of statistical metadata across surveys and statistical programs.

Knowledge of management principles, techniques and practices in order to lead a multi-disciplinary project team and manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment. Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management used at Statistics Canada.
Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata
Contextual knowledge: Advanced knowledge of Statistics Canada and Government of Canada policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, as well as other Statistics Canada policies, in order to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of all program activities and in order to explain policy requirements to clients and partners within Canada.

Knowledge of other statistical metadata management programs within Statistics Canada in order to integrate conceptually and structurally the statistical metadata required for various activities and programs.

Advanced knowledge of contacts within key client Divisions in order to establish a liaison; to evaluate and understand program statistical metadata requirements; and to provide expert assistance, advice and direction with respect to policy requirements, methods, procedures, systems, training, priorities and timelines relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to establish short-term priorities for the processing, storage, dissemination and evaluation of metadata across program areas and to effectively and efficiently direct metadata quality assessment projects, certifying and reporting to management on the overall quality, completeness, coherence and consistency of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives, organization, practices, policies, culture and priorities of Statistics Canada in order to ensure that these are reflected in the objectives and management of all statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems, and to explain the context of statistical metadata management at Statistics Canada to clients and partners across Canada.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act is required in order to ensure understanding and application of these Acts in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, particularly with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical metadata and other information; to explain legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media; and to ensure that Statistics Canada meets its commitment to ensuring confidentiality and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Research and analysis: Analyses and synthesizes diverse sources of statistical metadata in order to ensure that the quantity and quality of statistical metadata disseminated is optimal for Statistics Canada’s surveys and statistical programs.

Provides expert assistance, advice and direction to internal clients and external clients within Canada with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, determining changes in the needs of clients, assessing the impacts of these changes on statistical metadata programs and projects, and establishing short-term plans and priorities.

Analyses client requirements in order to determine the feasibility, procedural options, priorities, and target dates relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to ensure that approaches and results are consistent within, and across, surveys and statistical programs, and in order to direct and monitor statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes.

Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods, procedures and systems in comparison to those used elsewhere at Statistics Canada and elsewhere in Canada in order to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modifications or the use of alternative methods, procedures and systems which would result in operational efficiencies and/or improvements in the quality of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada.

Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats; to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals and to prioritize those updates; and to determine and mitigate potential short-term and long-term impacts on clients.

Analyses the quality of statistical metadata produced by surveys and statistical programs at Statistics Canada; evaluates current and proposed methods, procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata in order to develop enhancements; analyses gaps and inconsistencies in metadata quality and suggests possible reasons for variances among program areas; reviews the comparability of metadata over time in light of changing policy requirements, systems functionality and changing methodologies used by statistical programs; provides management with reports of findings.

Key Activities: Conducts research and comparative analysis on topics such as but not limited to: statistical products of different national statistical offices; data and information requests from multilateral (international) organizations; the scope and depth of involvement of internal subject matter experts in international activities.

Acts as the focal point or project leader in one or more of the following capacities: managing priorities and proposing feasible compromise solutions to meet the needs of multiple stakeholders in technical assistance projects; assesses the relevance and impact of data and information requests from multilateral (international) organizations, channelling relevant information to the appropriate internal expert community and reconciling and vetting responses and solutions prior to preparing and transiting a formal response back to the multilateral (international) organization.

Prepares and monitors work plan of activities to improve existing statistical products as part of a technical assistance project for other National Statistical Offices; writes/edits communication material such as detailed agendas, briefing notes, evaluation reports for technical assistance projects in statistics.

Coordinates and monitors the activities of a multidisciplinary project team working on approaches to improve the statistical products of a national statistical office for a technical assistance project with foreign countries.

Represents Statistics Canada in meetings with international stakeholders to discuss the progress of statistical capacity building activities being conducted in the course of a large scale technical assistance project with foreign countries. Represents the Division in discussions with internal subject matter experts about participation in international activities or working groups.

Provides advice and consultative services to internal subject matter experts participating in international cooperation projects in statistics; reports to the project sponsor (Global Affairs Canada, formerly Department of Foreign Affairs) and regional stakeholders on statistical products being implemented or refined through the technical assistance project.
Analyses the agenda items and recruits the appropriate expert communities to prepare briefing notes in order to provide to the Chief Statistician detailed and accurate briefing notes.

Communication: Gathers, compiles, analyzes and interprets information and data requests from multilateral (international) organizations, assesses the relevance and impact for Statistics Canada, and determines which expert community or communities should respond. Coordinates the delivery of data and information. Negotiates for deadline extensions or staggered delivery where appropriate.  Ensures that all necessary approvals are secured prior to delivery. All correspondence both internal and external is professional, polite, grammatically and factually correct, timely and archived using information management current best practices.

Prepares analytical reports and work plans in the context of international cooperation, to be shared with international stakeholders. Interacts with participating countries and regional stakeholders, providing mutually acceptable solutions to the challenge of simultaneously meeting the needs of multiple stakeholders.

Prepare written reports or supervise staff in the preparation of written reports for internal and international stakeholders, to ensure that they are informed of the progress of statistical capacity building activities being conducted in the course of a large technical assistance project with foreign countries (where capacity building means showing senior managers at other NSOs better ways of planning, managing and executing their statistical programs so that they will bring positive changes to their own organizations).
Makes formal presentations of recommendations, supported by original research, to senior management at Statistics Canada and senior management of other NSOs and international organizations.

Meets with senior management upon their return from multinational events, to gather feedback, status and direction on topics and issues in which Statistics Canada expert communities are involved. Analyzes and interprets this information, and presents it to the expert communities, soliciting their continued contribution and involvement. Researches and provides more background and supporting information for new or emerging topics.  Answers questions from the expert communities and ensures that they are in contact with the appropriate parties from other NSOs or multilateral (international) organizations.

The Chief Statistician of Canada attends several international meetings per year at which he actively participates in discussions about emerging issues of global concern (for example global warming or population censuses based solely on administrative data) or international partnerships on the development of new technology (for example how to exploit Big Data). In order to actively participate in these discussions, the Chief Statistician needs detailed and accurate briefing notes from Statistics Canada’s expert communities.  Each meeting has approximately 20 different discussion topics. These topics are very briefly described on the meeting agenda, which is made available typically a couple of weeks prior to the meeting. The position analyses the agenda items and recruits the appropriate expert communities to prepare briefing notes. The position supports the expert communities by searching the internet (sites of multilateral organizations such as the UNECE, UNSD, OECD, IMF) for background documentation, coordinating correspondence between Statistics Canada and experts from other NSOs working on similar topics, and providing other relevant information to the experts such as the governance structure of multilateral organizations or briefing notes from other meetings attended by senior managers.

Communicates orally with senior managers of other NSOs and multilateral organizations in a professional manner. Gathers and shares information relevant to the successful participation of Statistics Canada experts in capacity building activities, international working groups or senior manager level steering meetings. Provides written documentation to both Statistics Canada and external stakeholders of recommendations or results of studies or analysis, and progress on on-going activities.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic/sociologic principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of other regions (for example the Caribbean or South America) to initiate and conduct projects to improve existing concepts in other countries or develop new approaches to extend the application of official statistics internationally.
Knowledge of project management concepts, methods and techniques to determine the scope and depth of research and analysis projects for international clients.

Knowledge is required of computer software applications to conduct analysis and document project results, including specialized software such as statistical sampling, computer assisted techniques, automated working papers, and flowcharting.

Knowledge of social science research methods, techniques and practices, including multi-disciplinary analysis methods, to carry out analysis on a variety of approaches regarding the coordination of a national statistical system or improving relations between an NSO and other federal ministries.

Skill in synthesizing information from diverse disciplines (management science, economics, and public policy administration, etc.) to propose solutions that are feasible, reflect current best practices, and are multifaceted, addressing several challenges simultaneously.

Knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of consultation, management, small group process, interviewing and counselling to lead project teams, to negotiate contracts for services and agreements with other institutions.
Operational management requires management skills and knowledge of the theories and principles of general and project management to lead a multi-disciplinary project team.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge is required of the strategic direction, culture, structure and organization, mandate, objectives and relevant policies, procedures and practices of the International Cooperation programs and initiatives. This knowledge is required to achieve operational objectives and results in an effective and efficient manner, and to incorporate them into the conduct and management of studies and projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage subject matter studies and projects. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend improvements to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies and international organizations.

Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to the area of expertise in a statistical program (e.g. System of National Accounts, Education, Health, Labour, Prices, Demography, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). This knowledge is required to provide subject-matter advice, consultative services and to analyze and interpret data requests and assess their impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of other countries’ national statistical offices, multilateral (international) organizations (International Statistical Agencies) and non-government organizations in order to effectively communicate on approaches, methods, data and analysis for the purpose of strengthening statistical reporting.
Research and analysis: Analysis is required to understand and interpret requests for statistical information and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request.
Research gaps and overlaps in Statistics Canada’s involvement in international activities, and propose to senior management a strategic approach to achieving effective and efficient collaboration.
Conducts research and comparative analysis on statistical products of different national statistical offices in order to recommend areas of improvement.

Conducts research and comparative analysis of international contexts and statistical processes in order to recommend how Statistics Canada will respond and prepares and edits analytical reports, including recommendations for improving efficiency or effectiveness.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and to translate them into concrete and timely research studies. Conducts research and comparative analysis on topics such as but not limited to: statistical products of different national statistical offices; data and information requests from multilateral (international) organizations; the scope and depth of involvement of internal subject matter experts in international activities. From this research and comparative analysis, prepares and edits analytical reports, including recommendations for improving efficiency or effectiveness, and shares these reports with both internal and international stakeholders. At the outset clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with options, methods and techniques available.

Key Activities: Plans and conducts studies and/or projects using quantitative statistical data analysis methods, such as: data wrangling, validation, mining, and visualization (in R/RStudio, Python, SQL, Java, JavaScript or another software), as well as software development, application of machine/deep learning and artificial intelligence techniques for problem solving.

Plans and conducts the acquisition, analysis and integration of large statistical data sets from a wide variety of structured and unstructured data sources to identify patterns and trends contributing to the development of solutions to complex business problems.

Develops statistical measures and new data analysis techniques and processes, survey development, survey methodology, or components of data governance (e.g., policies, processes and standards, privacy, data quality, risk management) and on the use of data to optimize business value.

Plans and assesses the social, economic, fiscal implications of data to ensure that the development of policies, strategies, programs and other initiatives take into consideration the business foresight revealed from data analytics.
Plans and provides ongoing tracking, monitoring and reporting of the performance of decision systems and accuracy of statistical models.

Advises and briefs project teams, colleagues and managers on implications of studies conducted.  Drafts briefing notes, reports, and presentations, and contributes to the development and evaluation of position and policy papers and ministerial correspondence and/or Cabinet documents.

Attends Departmental, interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings to discuss data/information requirements, trends, gaps in information, problems, results, opportunities and effects on new or revised policies and programs.

Establishes and maintains client/stakeholder networks and expands the client-base in matters relating to data science and analytics, to optimize business value of data, to determine the implications on policy and programs and the decision-making process.

activities, skills, responsibilities and: Judgement is required to plan and conduct the research, analysis and synthesis of diverse data sources to contribute to the development of data analysis products.  When leading project components, judgement and latitude are required to make recommendations that affect the nature/scope of data science and statistical research/studies, including the objectives, approach, terms of reference, requirements, and methodology, where it is often necessary to adapt the methods for particular assignments.
There is latitude in the work when formulating and recommending new methodologies, techniques and analytical tools for the research and analysis of data.
The work may lead to improved methodologies, methods and processes used in economic, sociology and/or statistical analysis.
The work contributes to the preparation of discussion, position, and policy papers, briefing notes, and presentations for senior management, for use at Departmental meetings.
Judgement to discuss business information without divulging confidential information.

Leads/coordinates the work of components of project teams/working groups on a regular basis, recommend project scope, priorities, objectives, milestones, schedules, analytical methods and resource requirements.
Trains, assigns work and reviews progress of students and temporary staff. Verifies that contract work is completed and recommends payment.

Personal use and care of a computer and related software; standard office equipment, furnishings and supplies; reference material and policy documents; and multimedia equipment. May handle sensitive materials.
Uses taxi chits and travel credit cards for authorized business purposes.

Work concurrently with limited guidance on a number of assigned files involving identifying, assessing and linking a variety of complex advanced analytical information products and submissions, determining their value to work underway and upcoming projects, and weighing and balancing interests across all jurisdictions.

Choose the methodology and data sources and selection and/or modification of advanced analytical techniques to ensure that the outcomes are useful and meet national Statistics data requirements. Results of data science studies and the preparation of background reports and briefing material on the results of analysis containing interpretations and associated implications are presented to the Director for review, prior to presentation to senior management. Judgment and decisions have a direct impact on outcomes and consequently on the quality of advice and substance of Statistics program and policy decisions.

Apply advanced analytics principles including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization, and exploratory/confirmatory, predictive analysis, regression, and qualitative analysis, to understand the implications of analyses for the department’s policies and programs and to formulate conclusions and recommendations.

Review data collections and information sources to determine the usefulness of existing sources, to propose changes to the data collection approach and to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified methodologies, to identify and evaluate problems in the processing, editing, compilation and presentation of analytical materials, to provide solutions or recommendations to management, and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and methodological problems.

Plan and lead research and advanced analytics projects in the design, development and implementation of data analytic techniques, including artificial intelligence models and data visualization. Develop/prototype potential uses of these techniques to enhance STATCAN’s data assets and advance the evolution of analytics, reporting processes and data governance capabilities that generate more meaningful data in support of both operational and strategic, and program and policy decision making.
Create and test data and mathematical models for bias, of particular important in predictive and prescriptive analytics.

Drafts technical, position and policy papers, briefing notes, and presentations, which provide critical input regarding the economic and Statistics implications of data science studies. Participates in the preparation of reports to be submitted for publishing. This information is also used for planning and decision making for an array of key policies, programs, legislation and regulations by the Department and stakeholders.
Skill
Strong communication skills are required to establish and maintain networks across the branch and the federal community of practice to share best practices in advanced analytics.
Provides advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets.

Strong writing skills are necessary to prepare and present clear and concise analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science. Information must be impartial and clearly presented to minimize the potential for misinterpretation.

Discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur.

There is a requirement to liaise with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development, and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs.

The work requires thorough knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence, and exploratory/confirmatory, predictive analysis, regression, text mining, and qualitative analysis. This knowledge is required to optimize the use of the Statistics Canada’s data assets and to strengthen advanced analytics literacy. The work requires knowledge of the theories, principles, practices, and methodologies of statistics and mathematics in order to conduct the requisite modelling that provides meaningful information for policy and program decisions by management.

Thorough knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies, data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity.

Strong data literacy skills are needed to derive meaningful information from data, including the knowledge needed to read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data, as well as understand the use of data in decision-making and data-driven problem solving. Advanced data literacy includes data stewardship and the ability to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use. This is needed to formulate advice and recommendations on complex and sensitive issues/files.

Thorough knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of research is required including; hypothesis formulation and validation; model design and interpretation, experimental and comparative study designs; surveys, simulations, file reviews and case studies; qualitative and quantitative analysis including statistical sampling and cost benefit analysis; computer assisted analysis packages; and the strengths and weaknesses of these methods, tools and techniques in order to recommend and select project methodologies.

The work requires thorough knowledge of project management practices, techniques and practices combined with practical experience in planning and developing project proposals, business cases, project plans, schedules and reports.

The work requires thorough knowledge of the mandate, vision, values, culture, organization, legislation, programs, business lines and operations of Statistics Canada.  This is needed to ensure the alignment of the data analytics strategy with the department’s business intelligence requirements.

The work requires knowledge of the machinery of government to provide strategic advice on policy and program development, to engage in the system of multi-jurisdictional relations and to advance information and Cabinet Committees; knowledge of the roles and responsibilities of central agencies and partner government departments to anticipate multi-dimensional issues, participate in multi-departmental and federal/client/stakeholder project teams, and enhance knowledge sharing; knowledge of domains affected by departmental decisions; and knowledge of the positions, interests, priorities, structure and key officials of other organizations to support their engagement by STATCAN officials.

The work requires thorough knowledge and understanding of the governance structures of Statistics Canada’s partnerships in order to assess data provided by other levels of government for validity and integrity.

Knowledge of Departmental, Central Agencies and Library and Archives Canada policies pertaining to the handling, tracking, filing and storing of sensitive and confidential material and information holdings, including electronic records.

Supervises a unit or project team involved in the development of collection procedures and the capture, coding and processing of statistical data.

Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify operational systems and processes or explain program results.

Knowledge of statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.

Knowledge of other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of data suppliers is required to discuss data reporting agreements, as well as knowledge of data users from governments and the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on survey results.

Knowledge of questionnaire development to outline specifications and requirements for the collection and processing of statistical information and to provide feedback to subject matter experts.
